qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum number of HPC cores a researcher can use simultaneously with the SHARCNET Ansys license on Alliance clusters, both currently and after April 1, 2026?
qa_pairs.answer: Currently, a researcher is permitted to run a maximum of 16 simultaneous jobs using up to 512 HPC cores across all clusters with the SHARCNET Ansys license. However, starting April 1, 2026, this limit will be decreased to 384 HPC cores per researcher.

qa_pairs.question: What action should a user take if their Ansys job on an Alliance cluster fails to start due to a SHARCNET license shortage?
qa_pairs.answer: If an Ansys job on an Alliance cluster fails to start because it cannot acquire a SHARCNET license due to a shortage, the user will need to manually resubmit their job to the queue.

qa_pairs.question: Why might an Ansys job on an Alliance cluster fail to acquire a SHARCNET license, even if the user is within their individual core limit, and how can a user check the current license usage?
qa_pairs.answer: An Ansys job might fail to acquire a SHARCNET license even if a user is within their individual core limit because the SHARCNET license pool is oversubscribed. If all or nearly all of the 1986 `anshpc` licenses are currently in use by other researchers, new jobs may be denied a license. To check the number of Ansys licenses in use by your username and the total in use by all users, load the Ansys module and run the `lmutil` command, for example: `$EBROOTANSYS/v$(echo ${EBVERSIONANSYS:2:2}${EBVERSIONANSYS:5:1})/licensingclient/linx64/lmutil lmstat -c $ANSYSLMD_LICENSE_FILE -a | grep "Users of|$USER" | grep -v " Total of 0 licenses in use"`.
